_comment: Hand-authored. Aiming (direction to the player), direction to velocity, the sine table and the 8-bit division, bank 7 $F85D-$F9D0. The generators subtract these.

regions.name: Aim at the player and fly that way
regions.description: Slot $C0FC. $F863 (the direction to slot 0) and then $F8CE (turn that direction into a velocity for object X): the bullet and homing-enemy idiom. Called from $FE71 and through the slot. RUN on the harness.

regions.name: Aim: the vertical distance
regions.description: Slot $C0FF. In: X = the shooter, Y = 0 (the target is slot 0, the player's ship). $38 = 0 collects flags. dy = $0518,Y - $0518,X is made positive in $10 (flag $04 when the target is ABOVE, i.e. negative) and a zero becomes 1, so the division below never has a zero. Positions are the objects' own y and x fields, not their centres. RUN on the harness.

regions.name: Aim: the horizontal distance
regions.description: The same for x into $11: flag $08 when the target is to the LEFT; zero becomes 1.

regions.name: Aim: put the larger distance first
regions.description: If |dx| >= |dy| the two are swapped (so $10 is always the larger, $11 the smaller) and flag $10 is set: the line is more horizontal than vertical.

regions.name: Aim: the angle from a ratio, then the direction
regions.description: $F9B6 computes smaller x 256 / larger (tan of the angle off the major axis, 0-255). It is compared with the three thresholds at $F95B ($AB, $6A, $32 = tan 33.75, 22.5 and 11.25 degrees x 256, tried from the smallest) giving Y = 3 (within 11.25 degrees of the axis) down to 0 (33.75 degrees or more); Y OR the flags indexes the 32-byte table $F95E, which holds the direction 0-15. Out: A = the direction (0 right, 4 down, 8 left, 12 up, 22.5 degrees each); X unchanged; Y = the table index, NOT preserved. RUN: the 16 directions come out at every 22.5 degrees; a 910-point grid matches an independent model built from the thresholds, and 529 offsets match 'nearest of 16 by atan2' with no difference; a target on top of the shooter gives 2 (down-right); a target in slot 3 works the same.

regions.name: Direction to velocity: the base vector
regions.description: Slot $C102. In: A = the direction (AND $0F), X = the object. Y is kept in $38. The 16-bit vector is built from the sine table: y = $F986[2 x dir] -> $12 (sign extended into $10) and x = $F98E[2 x dir] -> $13 (into $11), i.e. 120 x sin and 120 x cos of the direction in 1/256 pixel. RUN on the harness.

regions.name: Direction to velocity: the speed class scale
regions.description: The object's $0698: bit 7 multiplies the vector by 8 (three shifts), bit 6 by 4 (two more); both give 32. The low six bits are the multiplier applied next.

regions.name: Direction to velocity: add it count times
regions.description: Zeroes the object's velocity fields ($05C0/$05D8 y fraction/integer, $05F0/$0608 x) and adds the scaled vector (low six bits of $0698) times. A count of 0 returns BEFORE this, leaving the velocity as it was. So speed = 120 x scale x count / 256 pixels a frame: $0698 = $81 is 3.75, $43 5.62, $82 7.5, $83 11.25, $C1 15.0, $01 0.47, $7F 118 - the gun's speed classes. RUN, all of these.

regions.name: Direction to velocity: restore Y
regions.description: LDY $38 and RTS (also the end byte the table below is indexed from).

regions.name: Aiming thresholds
regions.description: $AB $6A $32 = tan(33.75), tan(22.5), tan(11.25) x 256 (171, 106 and 50; the exact values are 171.1, 106.0 and 50.9). Read as $F95A + Y for Y = 3, 2, 1: the base is the RTS byte before the table, the overlap trick again.

regions.name: Aiming: direction by flags and angle step
regions.description: 32 bytes in four groups of eight: index = flags ($04 target above, $08 target left, $10 more horizontal than vertical) + the step Y = 0-3 above. Not swapped (vertical major): down-right 2 3 3 4, up-right 14 13 13 12, down-left 6 5 5 4, up-left 10 11 11 12; swapped (horizontal major): 2 1 1 0, 14 15 15 0, 6 7 7 8, 10 9 9 8. Step 3 is the pure axis direction (4 down, 12 up, 0 right, 8 left), step 0 the diagonal.

regions.name: Sine lookup
regions.description: Slot $C0F6: A = $F986,Y: 120 x sin(11.25 degrees x Y) as a signed byte (Y 0-31). Callers: the orbiting weapon in bank 6 ($88A0, $88B7: the Bullet Shield's position round the ship from a 32-step phase, the result scaled down by arithmetic shifts). RUN: Y = 4, 8, 16, 24 gave 84, 120, 0, -120.

regions.name: Cosine lookup
regions.description: Slot $C0F9: A = $F98E,Y, the same table eight entries on (+90 degrees): 120 x cos. RUN: Y = 0 gave 120, 16 gave -120.

regions.name: Sine table: 120 x sin(11.25 degrees x k), k = 0-39
regions.description: 00 17 2d 42 54 63 6e 75 78 75 6e 63 54 42 2d 17 00 e9 d3 be ac 9d 92 8b 88 8b 92 9d ac be d3 e9 then 00 17 2d 42 54 63 6e 75 again: a full circle of 32 signed bytes (peak $78 = 120) and the first eight repeated so that cosine = the same table read eight entries (a quarter turn) later, up to k = 31 + 8. The direction routine reads every second entry (2 x direction); the odd ones serve the 32-step phase of the orbiting weapon. CORRECTION: this was claimed as an 8-byte table 'whose meaning is not established' and a 32-byte structural-extent lead.

regions.name: Divide: Y / A (entry 1)
regions.description: Slot $C10B. In: A = the divisor, Y = the dividend. Out: A = the quotient, Y = the remainder (the 8-bit restoring divide at $F9BD). Callers: $D2DF, and the launch flight's pose cycle ($F370, $F3DB, which use the remainder). RUN: 10/3 = 3 rem 1, 7/7 = 1 rem 0, 3/10 = 0 rem 3, 200/1 = 200.

regions.name: Divide: Y x 256 / A (entry 2, the aiming ratio)
regions.description: In: A = the divisor, Y = the numerator. The dividend is Y x 256, so the quotient is the fraction Y/A as 0-255 (for Y = A it gives 255, not 256: 100 x 256 / 100 returned 255 with remainder 100 on the model). Called only by the aiming code, where Y < A always except for equal distances. RUN on the harness.

regions.name: Divide: the shift-and-subtract loop
regions.description: Eight rounds of: shift the dividend left through the accumulator, subtract the divisor when it fits and set the quotient bit in $11. Ends with TAY (the remainder), LDA $11 (the quotient).
